statement: file_id=GOV-00;file_class=GOVERNANCE;authority_level=0;governed_by=GOV-00;status=ACTIVE
violation: The root governance file lacks a canonical FILE-META record.
verification: Check first record of GOV-00 for canonical FILE-META statement format.

statement: GOV-00__SOURCE_CONSTITUTION__GOVERNANCE__GLOBAL.jsonl is the highest governance file for all governed control files and downstream artifact authority claims.
violation: Any governed control file or downstream artifact claim asserts equal or higher governance authority than GOV-00.
verification: Compare authority_level and authority claims across all governed control files and downstream artifact claims.

statement: The project uses AI-first JSONL rule ledger format for governance, source, index, build, and explicitly governed traceability/report files.
violation: A governed control file uses Markdown prose, headings, comments, or non-JSONL structure as controlling content.
verification: Parse every non-empty governed control-file line as one JSON object.

statement: Human readability is non-authoritative and must not override schema regularity, atomicity, or machine validation.
violation: A file adds decorative formatting, narrative explanation, or human-facing prose that changes rule interpretation.
verification: Check that rule meaning is contained only in fixed-schema JSONL records.

statement: Every control record must contain exactly these fields: id, file, class, type, scope, authority_level, statement, violation, action, verification, trace.
violation: A record omits a required field or adds an undeclared field.
verification: Validate each JSON object against the fixed GOV-00 schema.

statement: Field order must be id, file, class, type, scope, authority_level, statement, violation, action, verification, trace.
violation: A record uses a different field order.
verification: Inspect serialized JSONL field order.

statement: Each JSONL line must contain exactly one complete JSON object and no trailing comments.
violation: A line contains multiple objects, partial JSON, comments, or non-JSON text.
verification: Run strict JSONL parsing on every non-empty line.

statement: The id field must be globally unique, stable, uppercase, hyphen-delimited, and prefixed by the owning file family.
violation: A record id is duplicated, renamed without supersession, lowercase, or not prefixed by file family.
verification: Scan all governed records for duplicate and malformed ids.

statement: The type field must use one enum value from DECLARES, MUST, MUST_NOT, SHOULD, MAY, OVERRIDES, REQUIRES, FORBIDS.
violation: A record uses an undeclared type value.
verification: Validate type against the GOV-00 enum set.

statement: The class field must use one enum value from GOVERNANCE, INDEX, SOURCE, BUILD, CODE, TEST_OUTPUT, TRACE, REPORT.
violation: A record uses an undeclared class value.
verification: Validate class against the GOV-00 enum set.

statement: The scope field must be a non-empty array of declared scope tokens.
violation: The scope field is empty, scalar, implicit, ambiguous, or contains an undeclared token.
verification: Validate scope is a JSON array with at least one token declared by GOV-SCOPE records.

statement: The trace field must be an array of existing upstream record ids; an empty trace array is permitted only for root GOV-00 governance records explicitly allowed by GOV-TRACE records.
violation: The trace field references a missing id, contains prose, is omitted, or uses an empty array without root governance permission.
verification: Resolve every non-empty trace id against the governed record set and verify empty trace arrays are allowed by GOV-TRACE rules.

statement: Authorized scope tokens must be exact file ids, declared wildcard family tokens, or declared aggregate tokens.
violation: A record uses an undeclared scope token or undefined wildcard pattern.
verification: Validate every scope token against GOV-00 declared exact, wildcard, and aggregate scope tokens.

statement: Declared wildcard scope tokens are SRC-* and BLD-*.
violation: A wildcard scope token outside SRC-* or BLD-* is treated as valid.
verification: Compare wildcard scope array values against SRC-* and BLD-* only.

statement: Declared aggregate scope tokens are PROJECT, ALL_GOVERNED_FILES, AI_GENERATION, VALIDATION, CODE, TEST_OUTPUT, TRACE, and REPORT.
violation: An aggregate scope token outside the declared aggregate token set is treated as valid.
verification: Compare aggregate scope array values against the GOV-SCOPE-004 aggregate token registry.

statement: Declared exact non-range file scope tokens are GOV-00, SRC-INDEX, and BLD-INDEX.
violation: An exact non-range file scope token outside GOV-00, SRC-INDEX, or BLD-INDEX is treated as valid.
verification: Compare exact non-range file scope array values against GOV-00, SRC-INDEX, and BLD-INDEX.

statement: Exact authorized SRC file scope tokens are SRC-00, SRC-01, SRC-02, SRC-03, SRC-04, SRC-05, SRC-06, SRC-07, SRC-08, SRC-09, and SRC-10; exact authorized BLD file scope tokens are BLD-00, BLD-01, BLD-02, BLD-03, BLD-04, BLD-05, BLD-06, BLD-07, BLD-08, BLD-09, and BLD-10.
violation: A valid governed SRC or BLD file-id scope token is rejected because only wildcard family tokens are recognized, or an undeclared SRC or BLD file-id token is accepted outside the authorized range.
verification: Validate exact file-id scope tokens against authorized SRC-00 through SRC-10 and BLD-00 through BLD-10 ranges.

statement: AUTHORIZED_TYPES=[DECLARES,MUST,MUST_NOT,SHOULD,MAY,OVERRIDES,REQUIRES,FORBIDS]
violation: A record uses a type token not declared in GOV-REG-001.
verification: Compare every type field against GOV-REG-001.

statement: AUTHORIZED_CLASSES=[GOVERNANCE,INDEX,SOURCE,BUILD,CODE,TEST_OUTPUT,TRACE,REPORT]
violation: A record uses a class token not declared in GOV-REG-002.
verification: Compare every class field against GOV-REG-002.

statement: AUTHORIZED_SCOPES=[PROJECT,ALL_GOVERNED_FILES,AI_GENERATION,VALIDATION,CODE,TEST_OUTPUT,TRACE,REPORT,GOV-00,SRC-INDEX,SRC-00,SRC-01,SRC-02,SRC-03,SRC-04,SRC-05,SRC-06,SRC-07,SRC-08,SRC-09,SRC-10,SRC-*,BLD-INDEX,BLD-00,BLD-01,BLD-02,BLD-03,BLD-04,BLD-05,BLD-06,BLD-07,BLD-08,BLD-09,BLD-10,BLD-*]
violation: A record uses a scope token not declared in GOV-REG-003.
verification: Compare every scope field against GOV-REG-003, including exact SRC-00 through SRC-10 and BLD-00 through BLD-10 file-id tokens.

statement: GOV-00 overrides every governed file in governance, schema, hierarchy, naming, conflict, and modification rules.
violation: A governed file contradicts a GOV-00 governance rule.
verification: Compare lower-level claims against GOV-00 records.

statement: Cross-class authority order is GOV-00 > SRC-INDEX > SRC-* > BLD-INDEX > BLD-* > CODE > TEST_OUTPUT > TRACE > REPORT; INDEX precedence is limited to routing, classification, lookup, and ordering authority and does not create substantive source or build truth.
violation: A lower authority is used to override a higher authority, or an index file is treated as substantive source or build truth because of its numeric position.
verification: Check conflict direction against the declared cross-class authority order and classify index-derived claims as procedural or substantive.

statement: Numeric authority levels are GOV-00=0, SRC-INDEX=1, SRC-*=2, BLD-INDEX=3, BLD-*=4, CODE=5, TEST_OUTPUT=6, TRACE=7, and REPORT=7.
violation: A governed record or downstream authority claim uses an authority_level that does not match its declared file family or artifact class.
verification: Compare each record authority_level against its file family or downstream artifact class using the numeric authority-level registry.

statement: INDEX authority is limited to routing, classification, lookup, and ordering as declared by GOV-INDEX records.
violation: Index authority is used as substantive source truth or build truth.
verification: Classify each index claim as routing, classification, lookup, ordering, or substantive authority and reject substantive authority claims.

statement: Within a file family, the INDEX file governs routing, classification, lookup, and ordering for that family only; it does not create or override substantive source or build truth.
violation: An index file changes authority outside its file family, becomes substantive source truth, or overrides a non-index rule outside routing, classification, lookup, or ordering.
verification: Check index records against family scope and compare each index claim to GOV-INDEX limitations.

statement: SRC records override BLD records, code, and test output when source truth conflicts with implementation behavior.
violation: A BLD file, code file, or test output contradicts a SRC rule and is accepted as authoritative.
verification: Trace implementation claims back to SRC source rules.

statement: BLD records may constrain implementation only when they do not contradict GOV or SRC authority.
violation: A BLD record changes a source invariant, failure class, lifecycle rule, API authority, or schema truth.
verification: Compare BLD record statements against GOV and SRC records.

statement: Conflicts must not be silently merged, normalized, inferred away, or rewritten as compatible.
violation: A conflict is resolved without explicit conflict reporting and dependency stop.
verification: Search generated output for explicit conflict report records.

statement: When two rules conflict at the same authority level, dependent generation must stop until a higher authority record resolves the conflict.
violation: Same-level conflicting rules are arbitrarily ranked by the AI.
verification: Detect contradictory statements with equal authority_level.

statement: Generated code, test output, runtime behavior, or successful builds must not be treated as authority over GOV, SRC, or BLD records.
violation: A passing test, build, or implementation behavior is used to override a controlling record.
verification: Check reasoning path for code-or-test-over-document authority inversion.

statement: SRC-INDEX may outrank SRC-* only for SRC routing, classification, and lookup.
violation: SRC-INDEX is used to replace a source invariant, domain truth, failure class, lifecycle rule, API authority, or schema truth.
verification: Classify each SRC-INDEX-derived claim as routing, classification, lookup, ordering, or substantive authority and reject substantive SRC overrides.

statement: BLD-INDEX may outrank BLD-* only for BLD routing, classification, lookup, and build ordering.
violation: BLD-INDEX is used to replace a source invariant, domain truth, failure class, lifecycle rule, API authority, schema truth, or implementation constraint outside BLD routing and ordering authority.
verification: Classify each BLD-INDEX-derived claim as routing, classification, lookup, build ordering, or substantive authority and reject substantive overrides.

statement: Index files must not override substantive source truth or implementation constraints outside their declared index function.
violation: An index record replaces or changes a non-index source or build rule.
verification: Compare each index claim against GOV-INDEX authority and reject claims outside routing, classification, lookup, or ordering.

statement: Prior project chats must not override GOV, SRC, BLD, CODE, TEST_OUTPUT, TRACE, or REPORT authority; prior chats are context only unless their content is promoted into a governed control record.
violation: AI uses prior project chat content to override, modify, or justify a governed authority claim without a corresponding governed control record.
verification: Check reasoning paths, generated records, and authority claims for dependency on prior project chats without governed record promotion.

statement: INDEX authority is procedural-only even when its numeric authority level is higher than same-family non-index files.
violation: An index file uses its higher numeric authority level to define, replace, weaken, or override substantive source truth or build constraints.
verification: Classify each index claim as routing, classification, lookup, ordering, or substantive authority and reject substantive claims.

statement: Governed control file families are GOV, SRC, and BLD; downstream governed artifact classes are CODE, TEST_OUTPUT, TRACE, and REPORT.
violation: A new authoritative control file family or downstream artifact authority class is created without GOV-00 authorization.
verification: Check artifact family prefixes and authority classes against GOV-00 declarations.

statement: The authorized active governance file is GOV-00 only; duplicate GOV-00 variants are non-authoritative unless GOV-00 explicitly marks one as the canonical active file and all others as archived, superseded, or report-only.
violation: Multiple GOV-00 variants are treated as simultaneously active governance authority.
verification: Scan governed project sources for more than one active GOV-00 authority file or active governance variant.

statement: Authorized source files are SRC-INDEX and SRC-00 through SRC-10 unless GOV-00 adds another SRC record range.
violation: A SRC file outside the authorized set claims source authority.
verification: Validate SRC file ids against authorized range.

statement: Authorized build files are BLD-INDEX and BLD-00 through BLD-10 unless GOV-00 adds another BLD record range.
violation: A BLD file outside the authorized set claims build authority.
verification: Validate BLD file ids against authorized range.

statement: File names must use FILE-ID__TITLE__CLASS__SCOPE.jsonl with uppercase tokens and double-underscore separators.
violation: A governed filename uses spaces, lowercase authority tokens, missing file id, or non-jsonl extension.
verification: Match filename against GOV-00 naming pattern.

statement: The file field in every record must equal the owning file id.
violation: A record's file field does not match the file that contains it.
verification: Compare record file field to containing filename prefix.

statement: Every governed control file must include exactly one FILE-META record using canonical statement format file_id=<ID>;file_class=<CLASS>;authority_level=<N>;governed_by=<ID>;status=<STATUS>.
violation: A governed control file lacks one FILE-META record or its FILE-META statement does not match canonical metadata format.
verification: Parse FILE-META statement using the canonical semicolon-delimited key-value format.

statement: A FILE-META record is recognized by a statement field that exactly matches the canonical metadata format file_id=<ID>;file_class=<CLASS>;authority_level=<N>;governed_by=<ID>;status=<STATUS>.
violation: A validator requires the literal id FILE-META instead of recognizing the canonical FILE-META statement format.
verification: Identify FILE-META records by matching the statement field against the canonical metadata format.

statement: GOV, SRC, and BLD are JSONL control file families; CODE, TEST_OUTPUT, TRACE, and REPORT are downstream artifact classes, not JSONL control file families unless explicitly wrapped in a governed trace or report artifact.
violation: CODE, TEST_OUTPUT, TRACE, or REPORT artifacts are required to use JSONL control-file schema directly without explicit governed wrapping authority.
verification: Classify artifact as a control file or downstream artifact before applying GOV-SCHEMA rules.

statement: The project must maintain exactly one canonical active GOV-00 authority file in the governed source set; historical, draft, hardened, optimized, or alternate GOV-00 variants must be excluded from active governed sources or explicitly marked non-authoritative by GOV-00.
violation: A validation or generation run loads more than one active GOV-00 authority source or treats a draft GOV variant as governing authority.
verification: List all GOV-family files in the governed source set and confirm exactly one active canonical GOV-00 file is loaded as authority.

statement: Each rule record must contain exactly one enforceable requirement.
violation: A record contains multiple independent obligations that can pass or fail separately.
verification: Check each statement for multiple independent MUST, MUST_NOT, REQUIRES, FORBIDS, or OVERRIDES clauses.

statement: Each rule record must define violation and action fields that make failure behavior explicit.
violation: A rule states a requirement but lacks an observable violation condition or required failure action.
verification: Inspect violation and action fields for concrete failure semantics.

statement: The verification field must describe a concrete check, parse, comparison, test, or audit step.
violation: The verification field is vague, motivational, or non-operational.
verification: Classify verification text as executable, inspectable, or testable.

statement: Rule statements must not use banned vague modal phrases.
violation: A controlling rule contains banned vague modal language that weakens enforceability.
verification: Scan statement fields for banned phrases: generally, preferably, normally, try to, best effort.

statement: Rule records must not encode rationale as controlling content.
violation: A rule depends on explanatory rationale to determine enforcement.
verification: Check that statement, violation, action, and verification are sufficient without external prose.

statement: Controlled requirements must use positive enforcement or explicit prohibition rather than implicit preference.
violation: A rule expresses preference without a pass-fail boundary.
verification: Inspect type and violation fields for pass-fail condition.

statement: Registry records may enumerate multiple tokens when the record defines one registry boundary and every listed token has identical validation semantics.
violation: A registry record is rejected solely because it lists multiple authorized tokens under one registry boundary with identical validation semantics.
verification: Classify the record as a registry declaration and confirm every listed token belongs to the same registry boundary and has identical acceptance or rejection semantics.

statement: SRC-INDEX must route, classify, and lookup SRC records only.
violation: SRC-INDEX contains BLD implementation instructions, code generation steps, or BLD routing authority.
verification: Check SRC-INDEX scope tokens and record statements.

statement: BLD-INDEX must route, classify, and order BLD records only.
violation: BLD-INDEX changes SRC truth or governs SRC files.
verification: Check BLD-INDEX scope tokens and record statements.

statement: Index files must not restate governed rules except as routing references to stable record ids.
violation: An index duplicates source or build rule content instead of referencing record ids.
verification: Compare index statements against governed rule statements for duplicated controlling content.

statement: Index records must preserve lookup determinism by mapping query scope to exact file ids or record id ranges.
violation: A lookup path requires interpretation, guessing, or broad semantic search.
verification: Audit routing records for explicit target file ids and record ranges.

statement: Index files must include conflict escalation paths to GOV-00 for unresolved or cross-family conflicts.
violation: An index handles unresolved conflict without GOV-00 escalation.
verification: Check index conflict records for GOV-00 escalation action.

statement: SRC files must define source truth as implementation-independent requirements, constraints, authorities, and verification expectations.
violation: A SRC file contains implementation steps as controlling content instead of source truth.
verification: Classify SRC records as source authority rather than build instructions.

statement: SRC records must be implementation-independent unless the source truth explicitly requires a named technology.
violation: A SRC record unnecessarily depends on folder layout, framework mechanics, or code-level sequencing.
verification: Inspect SRC statements for build-only details not required by source truth.

statement: SRC records must expose falsifiable constraints suitable for downstream BLD and TEST records.
violation: A SRC statement cannot be checked, enforced, or contradicted by implementation evidence.
verification: Review verification field for a concrete downstream check.

statement: SRC files must not define AI codegen procedure, build order, commit order, or framework-specific implementation workflow.
violation: A SRC rule instructs file creation order, code generation sequence, or implementation procedure.
verification: Search SRC statements for build workflow terms.

statement: BLD files must translate GOV and SRC authority into implementation instructions without weakening source requirements.
violation: A BLD record omits, relaxes, reverses, or reframes a traced SRC requirement.
verification: Compare BLD trace targets to BLD statement semantics.

statement: Every BLD rule that affects implementation behavior must trace to at least one GOV or SRC record.
violation: A BLD rule introduces behavior without upstream authority trace.
verification: Validate BLD trace array is non-empty and points to GOV or SRC ids.

statement: BLD files must not create new domain truth, invariants, lifecycle states, failure classes, or authorized domain operations.
violation: A BLD record defines new domain authority not present in SRC records.
verification: Compare BLD domain claims against SRC authority records.

statement: BLD files may define implementation instructions only within GOV and SRC authority.
violation: A BLD file defines implementation authority outside GOV and SRC authority.
verification: Check BLD record statements and trace targets against GOV and SRC authority.

statement: BLD records must encode forbidden implementations when a source invariant can be violated by a common implementation shortcut.
violation: A high-risk shortcut remains implicit and unblocked in build instructions.
verification: Inspect SRC invariants and failure classes for implementation shortcuts.

statement: Downstream artifact claims in trace records or reports must trace to controlling upstream record ids rather than file names alone.
violation: A downstream artifact claim cites only a file without exact controlling record ids.
verification: Check trace arrays and report claims for exact record ids.

statement: Trace references must point upward or laterally only when allowed by GOV-00 authority; lower-authority records cannot justify higher-authority records.
violation: A SRC or GOV record traces to BLD, CODE, TEST_OUTPUT, or REPORT as authority.
verification: Validate trace direction against authority order.

statement: Reports must distinguish PASS, FAIL, CONFLICT, MISSING_AUTHORITY, and NOT_EVALUATED outcomes.
violation: A report collapses missing evidence into pass or silently omits unchecked records.
verification: Audit report outcome enum usage.

statement: Passing tests prove only tested behavior and must not be generalized into untested source compliance.
violation: A test result is used to claim broader correctness than its trace and assertion coverage support.
verification: Compare test assertions and trace ids against claimed coverage.

statement: GOV-00 records may use an empty trace array only when the record is a root governance rule not derived from another upstream record.
violation: A non-root record uses an empty trace array, or a valid root GOV-00 governance rule is rejected solely because its trace array is empty.
verification: Check that empty-trace GOV-00 records declare root governance authority and do not depend on lower-authority records.

statement: AI must load and apply GOV-00 before generating, modifying, summarizing, or validating any governed control file.
violation: A generated governed control file does not obey GOV-00 schema, authority, naming, or trace rules.
verification: Check generated artifact against GOV-00 records.

statement: For SRC work, AI must apply GOV-00, SRC-INDEX, the target SRC file, and all traced SRC dependencies.
violation: AI modifies a SRC file without required upstream and dependency context.
verification: Audit generation context list for required source records.

statement: For BLD work, AI must apply GOV-00, SRC-INDEX, all controlling SRC records, BLD-INDEX, the target BLD file, and all traced BLD dependencies.
violation: AI modifies a BLD file without controlling SRC authority or BLD routing context.
verification: Audit generation context list for GOV, SRC, and BLD prerequisites.

statement: AI must not fill missing authority with assumptions when the missing authority affects correctness, hierarchy, traceability, or build behavior.
violation: AI invents controlling rules where GOV, SRC, or BLD records are absent.
verification: Check generated records for untraced claims.

statement: AI must preserve existing stable ids unless the record is explicitly superseded by a new record id.
violation: AI renumbers records for aesthetic ordering or convenience.
verification: Diff record ids before and after modification.

statement: AI must emit machine-checkable output only when generating governed control files.
violation: AI includes explanation, caveats, headings, markdown, or comments inside governed control file content.
verification: Validate output as strict JSONL.

statement: AI must not include prose, Markdown formatting, code fences, language identifiers, comments, or conversational filler when a governed control file is requested as the final deliverable.
violation: The output contains prose, Markdown headings, triple backticks, language identifiers, comments, or non-JSONL text.
verification: Validate that every non-empty output line begins with {, ends with }, and parses as exactly one JSON object.

statement: Changing GOV-00 requires revalidation of SRC-INDEX, all SRC files, BLD-INDEX, all BLD files, code traces, and test traces.
violation: GOV-00 changes without downstream revalidation.
verification: Run full governed-artifact validation after GOV-00 modification.

statement: A changed record must preserve id when meaning is materially equivalent and must use a new id when meaning changes materially.
violation: A materially changed rule keeps the same id without traceable supersession or a non-material edit receives a new id.
verification: Compare old and new statement, violation, action, and verification fields.

statement: Deleted authority must be replaced by an explicit superseding or deprecation record unless the record was invalid JSON or duplicate noise.
violation: A controlling record disappears without replacement or deprecation path.
verification: Diff old and new record sets for missing ids.

statement: Modification output must include only the complete corrected file content when the requested deliverable is a governed file.
violation: AI returns partial patches that cannot be parsed as the complete governed file.
verification: Check deliverable completeness against target file identity.

statement: A governed control file must pass strict JSONL parsing before semantic validation.
violation: Semantic validation is applied to invalid JSONL.
verification: Parse every non-empty line as one JSON object before any downstream validation.

statement: A governed control file must pass fixed-schema validation before authority validation.
violation: Authority validation is applied to records with missing, extra, or misordered fields.
verification: Validate each record against GOV-SCHEMA-001 and GOV-SCHEMA-002.

statement: A governed control file must pass id uniqueness validation before trace validation.
violation: Trace validation is applied while duplicate ids exist.
verification: Scan all governed records for duplicate ids before resolving trace ids.

statement: A governed control file must pass trace resolution before dependency generation.
violation: Dependent generation uses a record with unresolved trace ids.
verification: Resolve every trace id against available governed records before generation.

statement: A governed artifact must pass applicable conflict checks before it is marked valid.
violation: An artifact is marked valid while an unresolved authority conflict exists.
verification: Run authority-order and same-level conflict checks before returning VALID.

statement: Trace resolution must occur after full-file record collection, not during streaming line-by-line interpretation.
violation: A forward trace reference is marked missing before the validator has parsed and indexed the complete governed file set.
verification: Parse and collect all governed records into an id index before resolving any trace array.

statement: A record with invalid JSON syntax has no authority until corrected.
violation: An invalid line is interpreted as intended authority.
verification: Run strict parser before semantic analysis.

statement: A missing required upstream file or record produces MISSING_AUTHORITY, not PASS.
violation: Validation proceeds as if absent authority imposes no constraint.
verification: Check referenced file and record availability.

statement: A detected conflict produces CONFLICT, not FAIL, when two authoritative records are mutually inconsistent.
violation: A validator reports one side failed without identifying the authority conflict.
verification: Report conflicting record ids and authority levels.

statement: A lower-authority artifact that violates higher-authority records produces FAIL for the lower artifact.
violation: A lower artifact conflict is treated as a source conflict when higher authority is unambiguous.
verification: Compare violation against authority hierarchy.

statement: Generation must stop when required authority is missing.
violation: AI continues dependent generation after required authority is unavailable.
verification: Check required authority availability before output acceptance.

statement: Generation must stop when same-level conflict exists.
violation: AI continues dependent generation after same-level conflict detection.
verification: Check same-level conflict status before output acceptance.

statement: Generation must stop when trace cannot resolve.
violation: AI continues dependent generation after unresolved trace detection.
verification: Resolve trace ids before output acceptance.

statement: Generation must stop when schema validation fails.
violation: AI continues dependent generation after schema validation failure.
verification: Run fixed-schema validation before output acceptance.

statement: AI must not optimize for brevity if brevity removes schema fields, trace ids, violation conditions, or verification checks.
violation: AI emits shorter records by omitting control fields or weakening validation.
verification: Validate required fields and enforcement strength after compression.

statement: When a choice exists between human readability and AI parse efficiency, AI parse efficiency wins.
violation: A governed file is made more readable by reducing regularity, repetition, or explicit control fields.
verification: Check for schema drift caused by readability edits.
